comments.text:
David, I saw this issue long before Tucker. Here is an essay I wrote to myself in August of 2023…three years ago…for posterity in anticipation of the inevitability of this issue being addressed:
There is a bipartisan solution to the two party dilemma we are currently faced with.  Now that one of those parties has rejected democracy and embraced authoritarianism, the time has come. Unfortunately, it would require a level of self-sacrifice by politicians and a temporary sharing of power that will never happen, even if it could save democracy. While a one party system might not be considered authoritarian if they are supporting democracy, neither is it democratic. 
	
It is not what our founders envisioned.  No one anticipated or considered what would happen if one of the two parties went rogue.  Now that one has rejected democracy, we are faced with a dilemma that nobody saw coming.  Well, both parties did see it coming. The Republicans have been trying to save themselves without changing their ideology in a democratic system that is no longer working for them, while the Democrats having been basking in the assumption that staying in power was becoming a sure thing. One way to save our country is through our existing democracy. If a third party is created and promoted, it is possible to shut down a rogue party by virtue of our election process.  If our political leaders, working together, strategically helped grow a third party with the realization that they might have to temporarily sacrifice political power, we could defeat a rogue party. Even if that meant the Democratic Party , privately of course, allows a new third party to win the 2028 cycle in order to establish themselves and possibly save democracy.  Working in concert with like minded people from both parties, whether currently or former members, a third party that believes in democracy could be started.  If the Maga voters represent 30% of voters, that leaves 70% of the electorate up for grabs.  Working together to promote a third party, the Maga Party could be shut down and with any luck never allowed to come close to power until a new election cycle when  a third party would be well established.

comments.text:
This is where the Australian system is superior. Preferential voting means you can vote for your more left leaning parties, such as the greens, but in the end, if the greens are not in the top two, your vote actually goes to your highest preference that is in the top two (for each electorate) .

So if the fight is between the two major parties, your preference of those top two is who your vote goes to...

Example vote for the greens 1st, but the Labor Party (democrats equivalent), if the greens come third on first preferences, your vote will actually go to Labor. 

That along with compulsory voting, means the party that forms government is the most preferable  to ALL Australians
